Emerging trends in light harnessing for CO2 reduction using photocatalytic MOFs
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction, mimicking photosynthesis, emerges as a promising carbon capture and utilization (CCU) approach. By deploying photocatalytic materials, including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), this technology permits to convert CO2 into fuels using light energy. MOFs, with their tunable structure, high surface area, and ability to incorporate co-catalysts, offer significant advantages for this process. However, a key challenge remains: inefficient light utilization, as many MOF photocatalysts primarily absorb UV light, a small fraction of the solar spectrum. This perspective article explores emerging trends in light harvesting strategies to overcome this limitation and maximize the efficiency of MOF-based photocatalytic CO2 reduction. We discuss sensitization strategies (dye, quantum dot, plasmon enhancement), MOF structure engineering (light-harvesting antennae, hierarchical architectures, thin films), and innovative concepts beyond single-photon excitation (upconversion, triplet-triplet annihilation). Improving light harvesting is crucial for unlocking the full potential of MOF-based photocatalysis, enabling sustainable CO2 conversion into valuable fuels and contributing to a circular carbon economy.

title: Programmed molecular self-organization directed by molecular Morse code
abstract: Nucleic acids exemplify the power of molecules to store and process information, as well as the remarkable consequences that can result from this. However, demonstrating such properties with other types of polymer remains challenging. Here, we propose an adaptation of the peptide β sheet motif as a system for storing binary information that is readable through selective self-assembly and has potential for informational self-replication. The scheme involves peptides containing both α- and β-amino acids, which can self-assemble into antiparallel β sheets if the α/β sequences match. The use of components of different lengths suggests the term "molecular Morse code" (MMC). The system is demonstrated in two sets of experiments, showing that intramolecular MMC can govern the folding of peptides into hairpin conformations and that intermolecular association to form hydrogels can be controlled by MMC, an effect that leads to self-sorting. Aside from its applications in controlling self-association, MMC could provide a means of coding information in the hypothesized "amyloid world" of prebiotic chemistry.

abstract: Summary Reversible self-assembly of supramolecular polymers plays a critical role in living systems, exemplified by the cell cytoskeleton. Analogous synthetic systems could be functional in the spatiotemporal control of chemical reactions, design of active matter, and energy storage for use on demand. We report here on an energy-storing supramolecular system that reversibly converts from small aggregates of molecules to supramolecular polymers. The aminonaphthalimide chromophore amphiphile monomer is conjugated to a methyl viologen moiety, that converts energy from visible light, chemical fuels, an electrochemical bias, or X-rays to store electrons and trigger formation of a polymeric pimer, accompanied by conversion from a solution to hydrogel. Supramolecular polymerization is synergistically triggered by p-p stacking and p-radical pimerization that stores electrons in the assembly. These electrons can be released, generating reactive oxygen species which proceed to oxidize an organic substrate in the absence of visible light thus providing a model system for dark photocatalysis.

title: Atropisomerism at the carbon–phosphorus bond
abstract: The feasibility of halting the rotation about a C–P bond is reported. At the outset, atropisomers with configurationally stable stereogenic C–P axes were synthesized in the form of triptycyl phosphine oxides with threefold stereogenicity. Their bond rotational profile revealed that each of the three barriers amounts to more than 115 kJ/mol, which permits the isolation of the antiperiplanar and the two enantiomeric synclinal C–P atropisomers under ambient conditions. Furthermore, the feasibility of their atroposelective synthesis by desymmetrization was established to catalytically control the configuration of stereogenic C–P axes. A first application of the synthesized C–P atropisomers was demonstrated by determining the absolute configuration of a protected amino acid.

abstract: The concept of covalency in chemical bonding is well established, but there are few methods to experimentally measure covalency, and none is a panacea. Quantum crystallography X-ray charge density determination could be the most powerful method for experimentally visualizing chemical bonding, but its stringent requirements have prevented routine implementation. Hirshfeld atom refinement (HAR) has begun to emerge as an alternative, potentially more accessible quantum crystallography approach for experimentally visualizing covalency, but its use has remained limited with heavy elements such as actinides due to challenges in partitioning and modeling core and valence electron densities in relativistic regimes. Here, we apply HAR to two extreme test cases of clusters containing three proximate heavy actinides exhibiting multi-center thorium-thorium bonding. We demonstrate exceptional agreement between experimental HAR and purely density functional theory analyses, thus visualizing the thorium-thorium bonding and paving the way to more routine use of experimental HAR visualization of chemical bonding.

abstract: Organopotassium compounds, though known for over a century, have rarely been utilized for organic synthesis because of their unmanageably high reactivity. We report a reductive strategy for the generation of organopotassiums from alkynes to achieve uniquely anti -selective borylfunctionalization. The anti -diboration reaction with a bulky trialkoxyborane proceeds with broad substrate scope in a conventional flask to yield the synthetically useful building blocks ( E )-diborylalkenes. Flow microreactors offer precise control, enabling unsymmetrical installation of a boryl and another functional group in an anti -fashion to furnish high-value, multi-substituted alkenes with excellent regio- and stereoselectivity. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal that the potassium-induced anti -selectivity, which is opposite to the sodium-induced syn -selectivity, arises from the larger ionic radius of potassium. These findings establish a principle for stereochemical control using abundant alkali metal elements and provide efficient sustainable approaches to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials.

abstract: Nitrogenases employ Fe-S co-factors to reduce the weakly π-acidic ligand N 2 to NH 3 . The Mo nitrogenase is more efficient than the V and Fe-only nitrogenases, but how the Mo ion enhances N 2 reduction is not fully understood. In this study, we undertake a comparative structural and spectroscopic analysis of synthetic [MoFe 3 S 4 ] and [Fe 4 S 4 ] clusters that ultimately reveals how the presence of Mo impacts the ability of Fe-S clusters to interact with π-acids. Specifically, we find that compared with the Fe centers in the [Fe 4 S 4 ] clusters, those in the [MoFe 3 S 4 ] clusters are more adept at backbonding to their weakly π-acidic N -heterocyclic carbene ligands. Such differences can be attributed to enhanced metal-sulfide mixing and Mo–Fe delocalization in the [MoFe 3 S 4 ] clusters, whereby the diffuse Mo 4d orbitals more efficiently transfer electron density from the sulfides to the Fe ions and, ultimately, to Fe-bound π-acids.

abstract: Of the three nitrogenase isozymes (Mo, V, and Fe-only), the Mo nitrogenase is the most efficient at catalyzing N 2 reduction. To better understand the chemical basis for this difference in reactivity, we herein study how the identity of M in an isostructural series of synthetic [MFe 3 S 4 ] clusters (M = V, Cr, Fe, Mo, or W) impacts the ability of neighboring Fe sites to bind N 2 . We find that only for M=Mo or W does reduction of the chloride-bound clusters result in the formation of an N 2 complex; those clusters with M=V, Cr, or Fe instead undergo bimolecular reactivity, with no evidence for N 2 binding. We argue that the divergent N 2 chemistry between clusters with 4d or 5d "heterometals" and those comprised only of 3d ions can be ascribed to electronic structure differences and that such differences may underlie the higher efficiency of the Mo nitrogenase.

abstract: Despite significant interest in enzymatic plastic degradation, the catalytic performance of currently available enzymes remains limited under industrially relevant conditions. Addressing this limitation requires approaches that can systematically identify the molecular features controlling catalytic efficiency and use this information to guide targeted enzyme engineering. Here, we simulate and contrast the catalytic activity of two enzymes, PETase and LCC ICCG , which are receiving considerable attention for their ability to degrade polyethylene terephthalate and related polyesters. These two enzymes have different properties. PETase has a more accessible active site but a moderate catalytic efficiency and thermal stability. LCC ICCG exhibits superior catalytic efficiency but requires higher temperatures to operate efficiently, associated with a less accessible active site. Using a new, efficient sampling method based on the committor function, combined with electronic and structural analysis, we characterize in great detail how both enzymes operate, identify the molecular reasons for their different catalytic efficiencies, and translate these mechanistic insights into the rational design of a double mutation (W130H and I179V) that significantly enhances PETase activity. This alters PETase catalytic behavior, promoting a mechanism similar to that of LCC ICCG , thus combining the best of the two worlds and potentially enabling efficient catalysis at lower temperatures.

abstract: Realizing the full potential of photocatalysis in synthetic organic chemistry demands detailed insight into its elemental reaction steps. For stochastic, rare and often nonuniform processes like charge transfer or photocatalyst deactivation, much information remains hidden in ensemble measurements. Methods with single-catalyst sensitivity are uniquely capable of uncovering such information; however, tracking individual catalysts under authentic reaction conditions remains challenging. Here, we present a single-catalyst operando photoluminescence spectroscopy technique for photoredox reactions catalyzed by lead halide perovskite quantum dots. The method achieves realistic reactant loadings and resolves particle-to-particle variations by directly probing individual catalysts, capturing signatures of charge transfer and catalyst degradation at the few-atom level. Case studies of synthetically relevant C-C coupling and C(sp 3 )-H bromination reactions help devising the mitigation strategies for catalyst degradation, while real-time monitoring of photocatalytic activities uncovers dormant states lasting several seconds. These results highlight the potential of addressing static and temporal heterogeneity in photocatalytic function to promote refined structure-property relationships.

abstract: Sunlight-driven photothermal water evaporation technology is currently reinventing the landscape of clean water and energy production. However, conventional photothermal evaporators primarily convert solar energy into latent heat for vapor generation, leaving the photochemical potential underutilized. This perspective introduces the concept of photothermal evaporation-coupled catalysis (PECC), in which the photothermal interface is augmented with catalytic functionality to achieve simultaneous sunlight-driven water purification and chemical upgrading. We first elucidate the physicochemical principles of energy partitioning for the synergy between solar water evaporation and catalysis and the materials chemistry principles for energy-efficient PECC design. Furthermore, we categorize the application scenarios of PECC based on interfacial reaction pathways, outline the unsystematized engineering principles of solar thermal management for PECC system integration, and finally propose the CLEAN paradigm to leverage the microscale principles of PECC and macroscale technoeconomic feasibility toward scalable, sustainable solar water-chemical factories.

abstract: As sulfide solid electrolytes (SEs) approach their intrinsic ionic conductivity limits, interfacial engineering has emerged as the key lever for further performance improvement. Organic molecular additives have therefore been widely explored to regulate interactions between SEs and their environment, as well as with lithium-metal anodes and high-voltage cathodes. Despite rapid progress, reported effects are often fragmented, and mechanistic understanding remains limited. This article surveys the use of small molecules, polymers, and supramolecular assemblies as organic modifiers for SEs, with an emphasis on how molecular structure governs interfacial chemistry, ion transport, and processability. By comparing diverse strategies across systems, we identify emerging structure-function relationships while highlighting unresolved trade-offs and open challenges. These insights aim to guide the rational molecular design of next-generation SEs.

abstract: The copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) is the flagship transformation of click chemistry and one of the most versatile reactions in modern synthesis. Yet its operational simplicity should not be mistaken for a single-species, universal catalyst. In practice, efficient CuAAC depends on matching the copper source, ligand environment, redox regime, medium, and substrate class to the task at hand. We analyze this paradox: CuAAC is broadly robust, but current platforms are only partially transferable across all applications. We propose this arises because productive CuAAC emerges from a cocktail-type ensemble of dynamically interconverting copper species formed in situ . Integrating mechanistic observations from homogeneous, heterogeneous, electrochemical, and biological systems, we outline a unifying view of CuAAC as a dynamic catalytic network. Recognizing this dynamic nature explains why optimizations are necessary and catalyst identity matters. This framework provides a mechanistic basis for developing wider-scope, more predictive next-generation click catalysts.

The bioconjugation proceeds under mild aqueous conditions, rapidly, and in quantitative yields, while preserving the structural and functional integrity of the enzyme. abstract: We investigated the light-induced behavior of different Cr-based antiferromagnetically coupled heterometallic systems. Time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance (trEPR) spectroscopy experiments using nanosecond-long laser excitation in the visible range allow for the observation of an intense, long-lived emissive trEPR signal, followed by a weak, absorptive signal persisting for hundreds of milliseconds. Wavelength dependence of the polarization inversion is investigated. We employ a theoretical model to rationalize the experimental observations and discuss the potential mechanism, in which the permanent exchange interaction and selective relaxation pathways driven by the modulation of the Cr crystal field play a fundamental role.

title: Molecular engineering of conjugated polyelectrolyte-enzyme biohybrid sheets for solar CO2 conversion
abstract: Bridging synthetic light-harvesting materials with enzymatic CO 2 fixation enables semi-artificial photosynthesis, but molecular design principles governing semiconductor-biocatalyst interfaces remain underdeveloped. Here, we establish a modular molecular design framework using conjugated polyelectrolytes (CPEs) as solution-processable, metal-free photosensitizers to construct photocatalytic biohybrid sheets through the spontaneous surface adsorption of formate dehydrogenase (FDH). Systematic variation of side-chain functionality and conjugated backbone structure reveals structure-property-activity relationships that dictate direct electron transfer at the abiotic-biotic interface. Molecular control over surface charge density, hydration environment, and long-range charge separation enhances CO 2 -to-formate reduction rates by more than two orders of magnitude. The optimized biohybrid sheet achieves a benchmark turnover frequency of 27,500 h ‒1 with stable operation over 48 h. These findings define actionable molecular design principles for co-optimizing optoelectronic properties and biointerfacial chemistry in organic semiconductors to construct high-performance biohybrid platforms for solar chemical production.

title: Catalytic atroposelective macrocyclization for constructing dominant rotors in peptides
abstract: Three-dimensional conformations determine the physicochemical and biological properties of macrocycles. Axially chiral biaryl fragments, which are widely found in macrocyclic natural products and drugs, have been evaluated as dominant rotors in synthetic cyclic peptides. While the corresponding constructs are powerful tools for influencing backbone conformations of macrocycles, their stereoselective installation remains challenging and underexplored. Here, we report a catalytic atroposelective macrocyclization strategy for constructing dominant rotors from azido peptides incorporating aryl alkyne building blocks via intramolecular rhodium-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (RhAAC). This macrocyclization delivers structurally diverse, ring-size-tunable macrocyclic peptides bearing triazole-based biaryl rotors with high atroposelectivity. Comprehensive NMR analyses, X-ray crystallography, and computational studies reveal key conformational features of macrocyclic products and elucidate the role of dominant rotors in dictating overall molecular conformation. This AAC-mediated atroposelective macrocyclization provides a versatile platform for accessing axially chiral macrocyclic peptides and expands the dominant rotor strategy toward stereochemically programmed conformational control.

abstract: Bridging the gap between molecular-level catalyst innovation and system-level process engineering is critical for the large-scale implementation of CO 2 utilization. This perspective demonstrates that traditional catalyst benchmarking, conducted using stoichiometric feeds, suffers from a recycle-reality mismatch: in industrial-scale processes, large recycle loops dominate the reactor inlet, creating highly non-stoichiometric, CO-rich feeds and shifting the thermodynamic equilibrium. Meanwhile, process models rely on outdated kinetics extrapolated into unvalidated regimes. By integrating techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessments across four catalyst families (Cu/ZnO/Al 2 O 3 , In 2 O 3 , InCo, and ZnZrO x ), we derive experimental catalyst-testing conditions and process performance metrics that reflect large-scale operations. We benchmark current catalytic performance and identify trade-offs between intrinsic activity, long-term stability, and the environmental burden of critical metal depletion. Finally, we propose an iterative catalytic process development cycle to align fundamental research with industrial deployment, accelerating the translation of catalytic breakthroughs into viable solutions for a sustainable chemical industry.

title: El Agente Quntur: A research collaborator agent for quantum chemistry
abstract: Quantum chemistry is a foundational tool for chemistry, materials science, computational biology, and others. Despite its power, its application remains restricted to experts due to methodological complexity, software heterogeneity, and the need for informed interpretation. To bridge this accessibility gap, we introduce El Agente Quntur, a hierarchical, multi-agent system designed as a research collaborator for computational quantum chemistry. Quntur follows three strategies: (1) reasoning-driven decisions rather than hard-coded procedural policies, (2) general and composable actions, and (3) guided deep research integration of quantum-chemical reasoning with software logic and syntax. Instantiated in ORCA, Quntur reasons over software documentation and literature to plan, execute, adapt, and analyze in silico chemistry experiments. Benchmarking against Claude Code in the same software environment shows that Quntur's domain-specific agent architecture more faithfully translates open-ended chemical requests into defensible end-to-end computational protocols. We outline advances, bottlenecks, and a roadmap toward an autonomous end-to-end computational chemistry research agent.

abstract: We report two organophotocatalytic dyads with distinct mechanisms that enable metal-free generation—and tame couplings—of transient carbon-centered radical partners. After forming their planar charge-transfer or charge-separated states, the dyads assemble non-covalently with radical precursors, and electron transfer reactivity is triggered by photoexcitation. Modulating the dyad's donor substituent diverts the mechanism from (1) consecutive photoinduced electron transfer via a radical anion catalyst/electron-acceptor substrate binary assembly to (2) a ternary assembly of a charge-separated catalyst and both partner substrates. In both cases, reductively generated alkenyl and alkynyl radicals couple with oxidatively activated trialkylamines in high efficiency, exquisite chemoselectivity, and excellent atom economy without the need for any transition metal co-catalyst—improving the sustainability of cross-couplings. Key to success was the intra-assembly generation and stabilization of transient radicals, preventing homocoupling/decomposition and furnishing a broad scope of products, including late-stage-functionalized drug molecules.

Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
abstract: Triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion can theoretically enhance photovoltaic efficiencies beyond the Shockley-Queisser limit. However, to achieve technological relevance, a transition from solution-based to solid-state upconversion is required. Such a transition has proven to be far from trivial, which raises the question of whether efficient solid-state upconversion can be achieved. Here, we employ kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, consisting of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. The triplet-state lifetime is therefore a key parameter in solid-state upconversion. We anticipate that these findings will provide insight into the key requirements for achieving efficient solid-state upconversion and represent an important step toward technological implementation.

title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
abstract: Biology uses folded polymer chains to perform complex tasks, from scaffolding catalytic enzymes to forming highly selective transmembrane channels. Aquaporins are quaternary membrane channels that exclude salts while transporting up to 3 × 10 9 water molecules per channel per second. Together with recently developed artificial water channels, they offer a potential route to less-energy-intensive desalination, an urgent emerging need. Here, we report extensively fluorinated aramid polymers synthesized by living polymerization that fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticles with well-defined, unbroken internal lumens. Continuous three-center F–H–F hydrogen bonds stabilize folding and create a polyfluorinated surface. These nanoparticles selectively transport water across membranes at exceptionally high rates of up to 4.5 × 10 10 molecules per channel per second, which exceeds natural aquaporins while retaining excellent salt rejection and water/salt selectivity of up to 5.4 × 10 8 .

title: Electric rectification by a redox-conductive metal-organic framework bilayer electrode
abstract: Abstract Unidirectional electron flow is essential for applications in electron storage and reconfigurable electronics, and traditionally realized in semiconductor junctions and even single-molecule concepts. Combining aspects from both technologies, redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) exhibit molecule-like behavior in a crystalline, porous matrix. Herein, we show that bilayer RC-MOF electrodes composed of sequentially deposited Zn(PMDI) and Zn(NDI) on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) function as chemical free-energy-based rectifying junctions. Unidirectional electron flow arises from thermodynamically allowed, and spatially organized redox reactions at the Zn(PMDI)|Zn(NDI) interface. Showcasing the rectifying function, electrons that reach the outer Zn(NDI) layer in the FTO|Zn(PMDI)|Zn(NDI) configuration are trapped as NDI•− and cannot be recovered by applying an oxidative bias. Introduction of [Co(bpy)3]3+ to the electrolyte creates a source–drain situation that reveals the potential-dependent directional electron flow across the bilayer. These results position RC-MOF bilayers as programmable electrochemical diodes, with rectification governed by layer sequence and redox accessibility.

Cellular protein delivery through cell-penetrating peptide-mediated water pores driven by membrane potential
abstract: Abstract Providing immediate access for functional proteins inside living cells would unlock unprecedented control over cellular processes; however, commonly used endocytic delivery suffers from endosomal trapping and degradation. One of the most powerful non-endosomal delivery methods uses cell surface anchored cell penetrating peptide (CPP)-additives that allow proteins to enter cells directly. Nevertheless, the underlying molecular mechanism involved in direct entry via crossing the cell membrane (protein translocation through the cell) and the major driving forces remain controversially discussed. Here, we provide a stepwise molecular picture on how CPP-additives enable uptake of protein cargoes through direct membrane translocation. CPP-additives accumulate on the cell surface in nucleation zones, locally hyperpolarizing the membrane, and induce transient water pores that allow selective CPP-protein entry without compromising membrane integrity. These fundamental mechanistic insights provide a firm basis for rationally optimizing delivery strategies using highly cationic CPPs, ultimately resulting in innovative and smart protein delivery strategies to advance therapeutic protein applications.
